title: One-tape self-simulation structure
statement: A particular self-simulation structure is defined with overhead function $t \mapsto (t+1)^2$. Its simulating machine is the diagonal simulation machine, and its decoder maps a binary code to the corresponding coded Turing machine. For each code, it simulates that machine's one-bit computations on paired inputs with a constant-factor overhead in the computation time plus input length; it also represents every language in $\mathrm{DTIME}(T)$ by a code whose decoded machine decides the language on every input within $c(T(|x|)+1)^2$ steps for some constant $c$.
caveat: The code-decoding construction is only referenced, not defined in the supplied descriptions, so its precise construction cannot be rendered further.
